issues.t: Oil sludge and engine failure (2.7L)
issues.sym: Oil pressure light, knocking, overheating, or the engine seizing, often with thick sludgy oil found at an oil change.
issues.why: The 2.7L V6 is known for sludging. Its internal water pump can leak coolant into the oil, and the engine runs hot on its oil, so neglected or contaminated oil breaks down and starves the bearings.
issues.next: Stop driving if the oil light comes on or the engine knocks. Change the oil often with the correct grade, watch for coolant loss, and have any milky oil checked right away.

issues.t: Stalls right after refueling
issues.sym: The engine stalls or runs rough a short time after filling the tank, usually when stopping or idling. It typically restarts.
issues.why: A float valve inside the fuel tank can swell from ethanol fuel and stick open, letting liquid fuel flood the vapor recovery system. Chrysler responded with extended coverage on the fuel tank.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Stop filling at the first pump click and do not top off. Have a dealer check the tank valve and ask about the extended tank coverage for your VIN.

issues.t: Early front suspension and tie rod wear
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, loose or wandering steering, uneven tire wear, or a steering wheel that is off center.
issues.why: These heavy sedans are known for wearing out front tie rods, sway bar links and lower ball joints earlier than expected.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected and aligned. Replace worn ball joints and tie rods promptly, since a failed joint can affect steering control.

issues.t: Takata air bag inflators (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. In a crash, a defective inflator can rupture and throw metal fragments.
issues.why: Driver and passenger front air bag inflators in these cars were recalled because they can break apart after years of heat and humidity. The affected cars are under a do-not-drive warning until repaired.
issues.next: Check your VIN right away. If a recall is open, do not drive the car; ask the dealer for a tow or mobile repair.

issues.t: Rear brake lines can wear through (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leaking near a rear wheel, a soft pedal, or a brake warning light.
issues.why: Rear brake tubes could rub against nearby parts and wear through, causing a fluid leak and reduced braking. Chrysler recalled affected cars.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Check your VIN for this recall. If the pedal feels soft or fluid is leaking, do not drive the car.

issues.t: ABS software can lock the rear brakes (recall)
issues.sym: The rear wheels lock or skid unexpectedly during braking.
issues.why: A software fault in the anti-lock brake module could lock the rear brakes. Chrysler recalled affected cars for a reflash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have it done before regular driving.

issues.t: Drive wheels can briefly lock during shifts (recall)
issues.sym: A sudden jolt or momentary skid from the rear wheels during a gear change at highway speed.
issues.why: Engine computer software could briefly lock the drive wheels during certain shifts above about 40 mph. Chrysler recalled affected cars for a software update.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the update done right away.

issues.t: Rear axle hub nuts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clicking or clunking from a rear wheel, vibration, or loss of drive.
issues.why: The rear axle hub nuts could loosen and let a half shaft separate. Chrysler recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Stop driving and have it inspected if you hear new clunks from the rear.

issues.t: Key can stick between Start and On and stall (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving, or the key does not return fully to On after starting.
issues.why: The ignition key could stay partway between Start and On, which can shut the engine off and disable air bags. Chrysler recalled affected cars.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for this recall. Make sure the key returns fully to On after starting until the repair is done.

issues.t: Front spindle nut may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or wobble from a front wheel. In the worst case the wheel can come loose.
issues.why: Some cars left the factory without a front wheel spindle nut installed. Chrysler recalled them for inspection.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Stop driving if a front wheel feels loose or noisy.

issues.t: Key can be removed when not in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The key fob comes out of the ignition even though the shifter is not in Park, and the car can roll.
issues.why: The wireless ignition node could bind and release the key before the car is in Park. Chrysler recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Always confirm Park and set the parking brake before leaving the car.

issues.t: HEMI lifter tick and camshaft wear
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping from the engine, often louder at idle or on a cold start, sometimes with a misfire and check engine light.
issues.why: The roller lifters, especially those used by the cylinder-deactivation system, can stop rolling properly. That wears the lifter and the camshaft lobe it rides on.
issues.next: Do not ignore a new tick. Have the engine inspected soon, because a failed lifter destroys the camshaft and spreads metal through the engine. Use the correct oil grade and keep up with changes.

issues.t: Broken exhaust manifold bolts (HEMI)
issues.sym: A ticking or puffing sound from the engine bay that is loudest on a cold start and fades as the engine warms up.
issues.why: The manifold bolts go through many heat cycles and can snap, letting exhaust leak at the manifold. It is often mistaken for lifter tick.
issues.next: Have the manifold area checked so a lifter problem is ruled out. The leak itself is not urgent, but it tends to get worse.

issues.t: Sudden alternator failure (recalls)
issues.sym: The battery light comes on, lights may dim, and the car can stall or refuse to restart. Some owners notice a hot or burning smell near the engine.
issues.why: The alternator on these cars can fail without much warning. Chrysler recalled many of them, partly because a failing unit could short internally and create a fire risk.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested right away and check your VIN for open recalls. If the battery light comes on while you're driving, turn off everything you don't need (A/C, radio, seat heaters) and drive only as far as a safe place off the road, not a long trip. If the temperature gauge climbs or the steering gets heavy, stop and turn the engine off. Your owner's manual may say what your car needs; follow it. The car can shut down once the battery runs flat.

issues.t: Left cylinder head valve seat wear (3.6L)
issues.sym: Check engine light with a misfire, usually on cylinder 2, plus a rough idle, ticking, and a loss of power.
issues.why: Early 3.6L engines could wear a valve seat in the left cylinder head, letting compression leak from that cylinder. Chrysler revised the head and extended warranty coverage on it.
issues.next: Have the misfire diagnosed with a compression or leak-down test. Ask a dealer whether any extended coverage still applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Oil filter housing leak (3.6L)
issues.sym: Oil drips under the back of the engine, a burning-oil smell after driving, or the oil level dropping between changes. Some cases also lose coolant.
issues.why: The oil filter and cooler housing is plastic and sits in the valley under the intake. Heat cycling can crack it or harden its seals.
issues.next: Have a shop find the exact source of the leak. Keep the oil topped up until it is fixed, and use an updated replacement housing.

issues.t: Overheated power center can disable ABS and stability control (recall)
issues.sym: ABS and stability control warning lights come on, and those systems stop working.
issues.why: A connection in the power distribution center could overheat and cut power to the anti-lock brake and stability systems. Chrysler recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Brake gently and allow extra distance until it is repaired.

issues.t: Headlamp wiring can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: The low beam headlights flicker or go out.
issues.why: A headlamp sub-harness could overheat at its connection and cut power to the low beams. Chrysler recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Avoid night driving if the low beams are failing.

issues.t: Side air bags can deploy unexpectedly (recall)
issues.sym: Side air bags go off without a crash, for example after a door slam or a bump.
issues.why: The side impact sensors were too sensitive. Chrysler recalled affected cars for a software update.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have it done promptly.

issues.t: Connecting rod bearing failure (recall)
issues.sym: A knocking sound from the engine, low oil pressure warning, or the engine quitting.
issues.why: Debris left in some engines could damage a connecting rod bearing. Chrysler recalled affected cars built from late summer 2011.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Stop driving if the engine starts knocking or the oil light comes on.

issues.t: Shifter confusion and roll-away risk (recall)
issues.sym: The car is not actually in Park when the driver thinks it is, and it can roll after the driver gets out.
issues.why: The electronic shift lever springs back to center after each selection, which made it easy to misjudge the gear. Chrysler recalled these cars and added software that shifts to Park if the driver door opens while in gear.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have it completed. Until then, always confirm the dash shows P and set the parking brake.

issues.t: AWD transmission output shaft can break (recall)
issues.sym: A bang or clunk, then loss of drive power. The car may roll if parked without the parking brake.
issues.why: The transmission output shaft on some all-wheel-drive cars could fracture. Chrysler recalled them.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Always set the parking brake when parked until it is done.

issues.t: Loose front driveshaft bolts on AWD (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or vibration from under the car, and in the worst case a loss of drive power.
issues.why: Bolts holding the front driveshaft on some all-wheel-drive V6 cars could loosen, letting the shaft disconnect. Chrysler recalled them.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If you hear a new clunk or feel vibration, have the driveline inspected before driving further.

issues.t: Cruise control may not turn off (recall)
issues.sym: Cruise control keeps holding speed after you try to cancel it.
issues.why: A software fault could stop cruise control from disengaging in certain conditions. Chrysler recalled affected cars for an update.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and avoid using cruise control until it is done. Firm braking still overrides it.

issues.t: Paint bubbling on aluminum body panels
issues.sym: Bubbles, blisters or flaking paint on the hood, fenders or doors, often along edges.
issues.why: Corrosion can form under the paint on aluminum panels. Chrysler published a service bulletin on inspecting and refinishing these panels.
issues.next: Show it to a dealer early, especially if the car is under warranty, before the corrosion spreads.

issues.t: Fuel rail hose can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell from the engine bay or visible fuel wetness.
issues.why: Damage to an O-ring and the fuel rail crossover hose could let fuel leak near hot engine parts. Chrysler recalled affected SRT cars.
issues.next: Do not drive the car if you smell fuel. Check your VIN for this recall and have it towed if needed.

issues.t: Oil cooler hoses can burst (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden oil loss, oil spray or smoke from under the car, and an oil pressure warning.
issues.why: The engine oil cooler hoses could fail and dump oil quickly, which can coat the tires or catch fire. Chrysler recalled affected Hellcats.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If oil sprays or the oil light comes on, pull over and shut the engine off.

issues.t: Engine computer voltage regulator can fail and stall (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving and may not restart.
issues.why: A voltage regulator inside the engine control module could fail. Chrysler recalled affected cars.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for this recall and get it done before regular driving.

issues.t: Wrong park lock rod (recall)
issues.sym: The car may not stay in Park and can roll.
issues.why: An incorrect park lock rod could stop the transmission from fully engaging Park. Chrysler recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Always set the parking brake until it is repaired.

issues.t: Side curtain air bag inflators can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning beforehand.
issues.why: A manufacturing defect could make the side curtain air bag inflators break apart in a crash and send metal pieces toward occupants. Chrysler recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have it repaired as soon as parts are available.

issues.t: Instrument cluster may not show warnings (recall)
issues.sym: Warning lights do not come on at startup or when there is a fault.
issues.why: The instrument cluster in some cars could fail to light its warning lamps. Chrysler recalled affected cars.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check your VIN for this recall and have it done soon so you do not miss a real warning.

issues.t: Windshield may not be bonded properly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing noticeable. Some cars may show gaps, wind noise or leaks around the glass.
issues.why: The windshield on some cars was not bonded correctly and could come out in a crash. Chrysler recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the windshield inspected and rebonded soon.

issues.t: Shifter can slip out of Drive (recall)
issues.sym: The car unexpectedly shifts out of Drive and loses power while moving.
issues.why: A problem in the shifter assembly could let the transmission leave Drive. Chrysler recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and get it done before regular driving.

issues.t: Parking brake may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: The car creeps or rolls with the parking brake set.
issues.why: The parking brake on some cars was not adjusted correctly at the factory. Chrysler recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Always confirm Park and park on level ground until it is fixed.
